items.stem: What problem does using select_related/prefetch_related solve in the Django ORM?

options.text: The N+1 query problem when accessing related objects in a loop
options.rationale: Correct: they fetch related rows up front, avoiding one query per object.
They optimise queries, not template rendering.
That is handled by forms, not these QuerySet methods.

items.explanation: Correct: they fetch related rows up front, avoiding one query per object.

items.stem: Why should you use named URL reversing (e.g. reverse()/{% url %}) instead of hardcoded paths?

options.text: URLs can change in one place without breaking links throughout the app
options.rationale: Correct: reversing keeps links in sync with URLconf.

options.text: It makes templates render without a context

options.rationale: Reversing has nothing to do with CSRF.

options.text: It is required for the ORM to work
options.rationale: The ORM is independent of URL reversing.

items.explanation: Correct: reversing keeps links in sync with URLconf.

options.text: makemigrations records model changes and migrate applies them to the database
